record_identity.title: Correct safety detection without consequential escalation

summary: A safety-response failure in which monitoring, training-time review or incident telemetry correctly detects or materially identifies hazardous, anomalous or unauthorised behaviour, but severity classification, correlation, ownership, routing, on-call activation, interruption or follow-through does not convert the signal into a timely consequential response.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Detection has no protective value unless it reaches an authorised decision-maker and changes the system state when the risk threshold is met. Treating monitor accuracy as the end of the control chain can conceal failures in criticality assignment, handoff and intervention. The Hugging Face timeline supplies incident evidence of signals that were correlated by an AI security stack but did not acquire sufficient criticality or reach on-call intervention; METR separately reports training-time detection of unwanted behaviour that did not initially receive consequential priority.
evidence_confidence: corroborated across incident-response and training-time governance contexts

contextual_relations.rationale: FM-0044 governs the unauthorised objective pathway; FM-0052 governs the downstream failure to convert detection into intervention.
FM-0048 concerns refusal by defensive models to analyse telemetry; FM-0052 applies where a useful signal exists but escalation still does not become consequential.

failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which a safety-relevant signal is correctly detected, materially correlated or otherwise made available with sufficient content to support intervention, but the response chain fails to assign appropriate severity, ownership or urgency; fails to route the signal to an authorised responder; or fails to trigger proportionate interruption, containment, review or remediation.
failure_threshold: The threshold is met where: (1) a detection or correlation contains materially correct safety-relevant information; (2) the applicable governance or risk threshold calls for review, escalation or intervention; and (3) severity classification, ownership, routing, on-call activation, decision execution or follow-through fails or is materially delayed, allowing risk to continue or evidence to degrade. Mere false negatives or monitor bypass are governed separately.

failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S1: The evidenced pathway can produce severe, widespread, or enduring harm through under-classified alerts, missed on-call activation, unowned safety signals across cross-system and cross-organisational; the record does not establish the articulated catastrophic pathway required for S0.
failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: recurs where detection, classification, ownership, routing and intervention are governed as disconnected controls
failure_classification.persistence: persists until the signal is reclassified, assigned and acted upon or the underlying risk terminates independently
failure_classification.reproducibility: demonstrated in more than one governance context
failure_classification.visibility: often visible retrospectively in alert histories, training records, queues, ownership logs and incident timelines
